Imputed Responses

Source: R/predict.R
imputed.Rd

Get posterior draws of the missing responses in fit$data. Use complete = TRUE to include the observed responses in each draw. For predictions of fresh responses, including at the missing rows, use predict(). See the missing data article for plotting imputations and completing your original data.

Usage

imputed(
  fit,
  complete = FALSE,
  summary = TRUE,
  width = 0.95,
  rate = FALSE,
  ndraws = NULL,
  draws_format = "tidy",
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

An mcpfit object with posterior draws.

complete

Logical. Include observed responses (TRUE) or only missing responses (FALSE)?

summary

Logical. Summarise the draws for each returned row (TRUE) or return individual draws (FALSE)?

width

Width of the central interval (strictly between 0 and 1), returned in the .lower and .upper columns. FALSE omits the interval. Used when summary = TRUE.

rate

Logical. For binomial models, return counts (FALSE, the default) or proportions (TRUE).

ndraws

Integer or NULL. Number of draws to select at random. NULL uses all draws.

draws_format

One of "tidy" or "matrix". Controls the output format when summary == FALSE.

...

Must be empty. Reserved for future use.

Value

With summary = TRUE, a tibble with .mean, .sd, and, by default, .lower and .upper. With summary = FALSE, a tidy tibble with .imputed, .chain, .iteration, and .draw, or a draws-by-observation matrix when draws_format = "matrix".

Tibbles include the original columns of fit$data and .row, the row number in fit$data. Matrix columns are named by .row. .draw matches the draw in as_draws_df().

Examples

# \donttest{
fit = mcp_example("missing", plot = FALSE)
#> NA values detected in 'y'. JAGS will treat them as latent responses and impute them during sampling.
imputed(fit, width = 0.8)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 8
#>        y     x state  .row .mean   .sd .lower .upper
#>    <dbl> <int> <fct> <int> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1    NA     8 B         8  35.4  4.45  29.7    41.2
#>  2    NA    19 A        19  15.5  4.30   9.99   21.0
#>  3    NA    27 A        27  17.2  4.34  11.6    22.7
#>  4    NA    28 B        28  39.4  4.30  33.9    44.7
#>  5    NA    29 A        29  17.6  4.40  11.9    23.3
#>  6    NA    30 B        30  39.8  4.39  34.2    45.3
#>  7    NA    31 A        31  17.9  4.43  12.3    23.6
#>  8    NA    68 B        68  41.2  4.45  35.6    46.9
#>  9    NA    84 B        84  34.6  4.37  29.0    40.2
#> 10    NA    96 B        96  29.6  4.44  23.9    35.3
head(imputed(fit, summary = FALSE, ndraws = 3))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>       y     x state  .row .chain .iteration .draw .imputed
#>   <dbl> <int> <fct> <int>  <int>      <int> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1    NA     8 B         8      1       1122  1122     32.7
#> 2    NA     8 B         8      3        681  6681     37.4
#> 3    NA     8 B         8      3       2856  8856     32.9
#> 4    NA    19 A        19      1       1122  1122     15.4
#> 5    NA    19 A        19      3        681  6681     16.8
#> 6    NA    19 A        19      3       2856  8856     15.6
# }
